publicationStmt.p: Tag layer of the DHSS Meta-Tagging Project. The article text is reproduced from the staged copy named in sourceDesc and is not altered; the tags are held separately in standOff so that overlapping and nested spans are preserved.

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: method
span.quote: With regard to the monitoring of consciousness, both the AMLR and 40 Hz ASSR provide a reliable indication of the presence or absence of consciousness in subjects receiving a general anesthetic agent.

span.label: auditory evoked potentials as a measure of anaesthetic depth
span.quote: Auditory evoked potentials (AEPs) are changes of the electrical activity of the brain (i.e. the electroencephalogram—EEG), produced by auditory stimuli.

span.label: review
span.quote: We will review their physiological basis, the recording methodology, the effects of general anesthetics, their ability to track changes in level of consciousness and their clinical applications.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: at ~40 stimuli per second each new stimulus arrives during wave Pa of the preceding response, so successive middle-latency responses overlap and progressively build up into the steady-state response
span.quote: With stimulus rates near 40/second, the next stimulus occurs during wave Pa of the AMLR evoked by the preceding stimuli, thus allowing progressive build-up of the 40 Hz ASSR by superimposition of the individual AMLR.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: the 40 Hz ASSR is generated partly by anesthetic-sensitive synchronization of naturally occurring neuronal rhythms, and/or anesthetics disrupt the superimposition process by non-uniformly changing the refractory periods of AMLR components
span.quote: This therefore suggests that the 40 Hz ASSR partly arises from synchronization of naturally occurring neuronal rhythms63 (that are affected by general anesthetics64) or that general anesthetics interfere with the superimposition process (possibly by not uniformly affecting the refractory period of the AMLR components).

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: general anesthetics abolish consciousness by interfering with thalamocortical 40 Hz rhythms, which is why the 40 Hz response and consciousness disappear together
span.quote: An example is the hypothesis66 that general anesthetics impair consciousness by interfering with thalamocortical 40 Hz rhythms.

span.label: Scope restricted to human studies for reasons of space
span.note: what this limits: the scope of the review: BECAUSE OF SPACE CONSTRAINTS, THIS REVIEW WILL BE LIMITED TO HUMAN STUDIES
span.quote: Because of space constraints, this review will be limited to human studies.

span.label: The association between ASSR attenuation and loss of consciousness is correlational, not demonstrated to be functional
span.note: what this limits: any use of the 40 Hz ASSR as a consciousness monitor: THESE OBSERVATIONS SUGGEST BUT DO NOT PROVE THAT THERE IS FUNCTIONAL RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN THE ATTENUATION OF THE 40 HZ ASSR AND LOSS OF CONSCIOUSNESS
span.quote: These observations suggest but do not prove that there is functional relationship between the attenuation of the 40 Hz ASSR and loss of consciousness.

span.label: Applicability to real-world multi-drug anaesthetic regimens is untested
span.note: what this limits: clinical application specifically: APPLICABILITY [to the] MULTI-DRUG REGIMEN COMMONLY SEEN IN CLINICAL PRACTICE REMAINS TO BE ASSESSED
span.quote: Applicability multi-drug regimen commonly seen in clinical practice remains to be assessed, as for BIS and other monitoring modalities.71

span.label: Whether ASSR parameters other than amplitude could support titration has not been examined
span.note: what this limits: the amplitude measure only: whether ASSR parameters other than amplitude could support titration has not been examined
span.quote: Whether other parameters of the ASSR (phase alone or combined with amplitude, use of either stimulation frequencies.) could be useful has not been examined.

span.label: The monitor and the patient's state may both be effects of the drug rather than related to each other, and the review says so of its own subject.
span.note: what this limits: a 40 Hz ASSR or AMLR reading used to infer that a patient is unconscious: the review states both the response and the loss of consciousness could be effects of the anaesthetic that are otherwise functionally independent
span.quote: Loss of consciousness and attenuation of the 40 Hz ASSR (or of the AMLR, BIS,.) could, however, be effects that both result from the presence of the anesthetic in the brain but that are otherwise functionally independent.

span.label: The supporting evidence is explicitly said to fall short of proof.
span.note: what this limits: the claim that attenuation of the 40 Hz ASSR indicates loss of consciousness: the review states the observations suggest but do not prove a functional relationship
span.quote: These observations suggest but do not prove that there is functional relationship

span.label: Whole components of the response are excluded from clinical use for being TOO sensitive, so the monitored signal is selected for stability rather than for sensitivity.
span.note: what this limits: the auditory evoked potentials used in anaesthetic monitoring: slow and late responses are excluded as too sensitive to anaesthetic effect for routine clinical monitoring
span.quote: The slow and late responses reflect higher level of processing and are considered too sensitive to anesthetic effect for routine clinical monitoring and will not be discussed here further.

span.label: 40 Hz ASSR
span.quote: The above evidence collectively suggests that the 40 Hz ASSR provides a fairly reliable measure of the level of consciousness.

span.label: level of consciousness
span.quote: These observations suggest but do not prove that there is functional relationship between the attenuation of the 40 Hz ASSR and loss of consciousness.

span.label: auditory middle latency response
span.quote: The auditory middle latency response (10–50 millisecond) (AMLR) (Figure 1) is, by far, the EP most commonly used to measure anesthetic effect.

span.label: 40 Hz ASSR as an index of consciousness - AS CORRELATION: a fairly reliable measure of the level of consciousness, on evidence the review calls suggestive but not probative
span.quote: The above evidence collectively suggests that the 40 Hz ASSR provides a fairly reliable measure of the level of consciousness.

span.label: 40 Hz ASSR as an index of consciousness - AS TESTED BY DISSOCIATION: consciousness was restored with the anaesthetic concentration held constant, and the response returned to awake baseline
span.quote: Physostigmine restored consciousness in 10 of 11 volunteers who had been rendered unconscious by propofol. In the 10 subjects who regained consciousness, there was a concomitant increase of the 40 Hz ASSR to awake baseline values.

span.label: contradicts → Pockett et al.3
span.quote: Presence of PAMR led Pockett et al3 to conclude erroneously4 that the 40 Hz ASSR is not a suitable monitor of anesthesia.

span.label: contradicts → Galambos et al.42 (the 40 Hz ASSR as superimposition of the AMLR)
span.quote: We have examined the effect of enflurane/N2O anesthesia on the AMLR and 40 Hz ASSR and found that attenuation of the 40 Hz ASSR was much more pronounced that predicted by alterations of the AMLR.52

span.label: level of consciousness —operationalised-as→ 40 Hz ASSR
span.quote: The above evidence collectively suggests that the 40 Hz ASSR provides a fairly reliable measure of the level of consciousness.

span.label: statistical significance test
span.quote: There was a modest but statistically significant increase in the amplitude of the 40 Hz ASSR in the five subjects who showed a behavioral change.

span.label: mean (signal averaging across trials)
span.quote: Each tracing represents the average of 1000 responses.

span.label: Most volatile and intravenous general anesthetics lengthen the latency and reduce the amplitude of the auditory middle latency response, and do so in proportion to concentration.
span.quote: There is ample evidence that most general anesthetics (halothane, enflurane, isoflurane, desflurane, sevoflurane, propofol, etomidate, althesin, xenon) increase the latency and decreased the amplitude of the AMLR in a concentration-dependent manner.

span.label: Nitrous oxide and ketamine leave the main AMLR components unchanged even at concentrations that abolish consciousness, so the AMLR does not track consciousness under these two drugs.
span.quote: N2O15 and ketamine17 cause no change of the main components of the AMLR, even at concentrations producing unconsciousness.

span.label: Ketamine raises rather than lowers the amplitude of the 40 Hz steady-state response, opposite to every other anesthetic reviewed.
span.quote: Unlike other anesthetics, ketamine increased the amplitude of the 40 Hz ASSR.

span.label: Reversing anesthetic hypnosis with physostigmine while the anesthetic concentration is held constant brings the 40 Hz ASSR back in proportion to the behavioural reversal, indicating that ASSR attenuation reflects impaired consciousness rather than mere drug presence.
span.quote: The attenuation of the 40 Hz ASSR by general anesthetics thus seems to reflect the impairment of consciousness since, antagonism of the hypnotic effect of the anesthetics by physostigmine is associated with an increase in the amplitude of the 40 Hz ASSR that matches the magnitude of the hypnotic reversal.

span.label: Under enflurane/N2O the 40 Hz ASSR was suppressed far more than could be predicted from the accompanying AMLR changes, so the steady-state response cannot be merely the sum of overlapping middle-latency responses.
span.quote: We have examined the effect of enflurane/N2O anesthesia on the AMLR and 40 Hz ASSR and found that attenuation of the 40 Hz ASSR was much more pronounced that predicted by alterations of the AMLR.

span.label: The 40 Hz ASSR amplitude cannot be used to titrate anesthetic dose once consciousness is lost because it is already almost fully suppressed at that point.
span.quote: The amplitude 40 Hz ASSR does not appear useful for titration because it is already markedly reduced at loss of consciousness.

span.label: Noxious stimulation increases AMLR-derived measures, so the AMLR indexes the net balance between anesthetic suppression and stimulation-driven brain activation rather than anesthetic depth alone.
span.quote: These observations suggest that the AMLR reflects the balance between anesthetic suppression and brain activation caused by noxious stimulation.

span.label: auditory evoked potential (AEP)
span.quote: Auditory evoked potentials (AEPs) are changes of the electrical activity of the brain (i.e. the electroencephalogram—EEG), produced by auditory stimuli.

span.label: transient AEP
span.quote: Transient AEPs are seen when rate of stimulus delivery is slow enough for the response to wear off before the next stimulus.

span.label: steady-state AEP
span.quote: Steady-state AEPs are seen when rate of stimulus delivery is fast enough to cause overlap of the individual transient responses.

span.label: 40 Hz auditory steady-state response (40 Hz ASSR)
span.term: 40 Hz auditory steady-state response (40 Hz ASSR)
span.quote: The 40 Hz ASSR is a sustained, sinusoidal electrical response of the brain to auditory stimuli delivered at rates near 40 Hz

span.label: auditory middle latency response (AMLR)
span.quote: The AMLR consists of three main peaks: Na, Pa and Nb with nominal latency in awake subjects of 15–20, 25–30 and 40 millisecond, respectively

span.label: coherent frequency (CF)
span.quote: Munglani et al58 examined the effect of isoflurane (0–0.8%) on the stimulus rate producing the largest ASSR with little or no power in the harmonics, rate called the coherent frequency (CF).

span.label: unintentional awareness
span.quote: The use of neuromuscular blocking drugs carries the risk of unintentional awareness during anesthesia, i.e. the accidental regaining of consciousness during surgery by a patient who is paralyzed and thus unable to signal his or her discomfort.

span.label: A-Line ARX index (AAI)
span.quote: The device also provide an index (A- Line ARX index—AAI) defined as the sum of absolute differences in the 20– 80 millisecond window of the AMLR.

span.label: physostigmine administration (cholinesterase inhibitor given to antagonize hypnosis)
span.term: physostigmine administration (cholinesterase inhibitor given to antagonize hypnosis)
span.quote: In an attempt to establish a stronger link 40 Hz ASSR and the level of consciousness, we have used physostigmine (a central acting cholinesterase inhibitor) to antagonize the hypnotic effects of propofol59 and sevoflurane57 while keeping the concentration of the anesthetic constant.

span.label: anesthetic concentration (held constant during the physostigmine reversal)
span.term: anesthetic concentration (held constant during the physostigmine reversal)
span.quote: In an attempt to establish a stronger link 40 Hz ASSR and the level of consciousness, we have used physostigmine (a central acting cholinesterase inhibitor) to antagonize the hypnotic effects of propofol59 and sevoflurane57 while keeping the concentration of the anesthetic constant.

span.label: inhaled isoflurane concentration (0–0.5%)
span.quote: A study with human volunteers55 showed that the 40 Hz ASSR is attenuated in a concentration-dependent manner by isoflurane 0–0.5%; that the attenuation is nearly maximal at 0.5% isoflurane; that the 40 Hz ASSR is an excellent predictor of the level of consciousness.

span.label: 40 Hz ASSR amplitude
span.quote: There was a modest but statistically significant increase in the amplitude of the 40 Hz ASSR in the five subjects who showed a behavioral change.

span.label: level of consciousness (ability to follow verbal commands)
span.term: level of consciousness (ability to follow verbal commands)
span.quote: Physostigmine restored consciousness in 10 of 11 volunteers who had been rendered unconscious by propofol.

span.label: 2.1 ng/ml — sufentanil concentration producing half-maximal suppression of the 40 Hz ASSR
span.quote: The sufentanil IC50 was 2.1 ng/ml.

span.label: more than 70% — reduction in 40 Hz ASSR amplitude when sevoflurane was titrated to unconsciousness (mean 0.85% end-tidal)
span.quote: Unconsciousness induced by individual titration of sevoflurane (mean 0.85% end-tidal concentration) reduced the ASSR amplitude by more than 70%,

span.label: about 33 Hz / 15 Hz — coherent frequency of the steady-state response when awake versus when unconscious
span.quote: The CF is about 33 Hz in awake subjects and 15 Hz during unconsciousness.

span.label: z20% — reduction of the A-Line ARX index caused by the neuromuscular blocker vecuronium during steady-state anesthesia (i.e. muscle-artefact contribution to the index)
span.quote: Ge et al showed that the AAI is reduced by vecuronium by z20% during steady-state anesthesia in patients without surgical stimuli.

span.label: 10 of 11 — propofol-anesthetized volunteers in whom physostigmine restored consciousness
span.quote: Physostigmine restored consciousness in 10 of 11 volunteers who had been rendered unconscious by propofol.

span.label: two of eight — sevoflurane-anesthetized subjects who regained consciousness after physostigmine (three more regained wakefulness only)
span.quote: Of eight subjects, two regained consciousness, three regained wakefulness (they opened their eyes but did not follow verbal commands) and three showed no behavioral changes.
